descriptor.scene: DAVID KOBROSKY, chest-up at his crowded kitchen counter, hands a tall fruit smoothie across to a guest whose hands are just receiving it, HIS EYES LOCKED ON THE GUEST'S EYES, both mid-laugh. The blender jug sits beside him with three more filled glasses lined up, each a different sunrise color. Behind him, slightly soft, a wall crowded with dozens of small pinned photographs of past brunches, years of them, and a small glass jar of wooden tokens on the shelf. The guest is seen from behind over their shoulder, softly out of focus. Warm morning light. Lower-right: countertop with a folded dish towel, calm.
descriptor._caption: He ran Brunch Club for years, more than a hundred brunches in all, and he made the smoothies himself. Ask anyone who came. The room stayed small on purpose, the door stayed open anyway, and table by table he became the center of a certain kind of gravity in New York.
descriptor.anonymous: One guest receiving the smoothie, seen mostly from behind: a young woman with a dark ponytail in a green cardigan, visibly distinct from David.
negatives: legible text on the photographs or tokens
